JERA Announces Update to Planned Transfer of Participating Interests in the Ichthys LNG Project 2026/09/25
JERA Co., Inc. (JERA) today announced an update to the previously announced transfer of its interests in the Ichthys LNG Project, held through its subsidiary JERA Australia Pty Ltd. The interest will be transferred to Australian subsidiaries of INPEX CORPORATION (INPEX), following INPEX’s exercise of its pre-emptive rights to acquire JERA’s participating interest in this project.
On March 12, 2026, JERA announced that it had agreed to transfer its interest in the Ichthys LNG Project (0.735%) and the Gorgon LNG Project (0.417%) to MidOcean Energy ( announcement here ). During the transaction process, INPEX exercised its pre-emptive rights under the applicable shareholders’ agreement with respect to JERA’s interest in the Ichthys LNG Project. The planned transfer of JERA’s interest in the Gorgon LNG Project to MidOcean Energy remains unchanged.
The transfer of JERA’s interest in the Ichthys LNG Project will have no impact on JERA’s LNG procurement. As part of its commitment to supporting Japan’s energy security, JERA will continue to procure LNG from the Ichthys LNG Project under its existing LNG sale and purchase agreements. JERA will also continue to procure LNG from the Gorgon LNG Project following completion of the previously announced transfer of its interest in that project.
Australia remains a strategically important partner and a trusted and reliable source of LNG for JERA. The company remains committed to its Australian LNG portfolio and to its major investments in Australia, including the Wheatstone LNG Project, the Barossa Gas Project, and the Scarborough Energy Project. Through its extensive experience across the LNG value chain, JERA will continue to contribute to Japan's energy security and support a stable, affordable, and lower-carbon energy future.
About JERA JERA is a global energy leader and Japan’s largest power generation company focused on providing cutting-edge solutions to the world's energy issues. Established in 2015, the company produces one-third of Japan’s electricity and is one of the largest LNG buyers in the world. JERA has global reach and strength throughout the energy supply chain, including participation in upstream gas exploration and production, LNG projects, fuel procurement and transportation, and power generation globally. In support of a responsible energy transition, JERA aims to achieve net-zero CO₂ emissions from its domestic and overseas businesses by 2050.
